statusDetail: Atomic coverage is complete. Three linked representative destinations returned CloudFront 403 responses; those observed site failures are findings rather than untested checks.

paths.description: Public homepage and primary multimodal route-search entry. Represents global chrome, the highest-traffic task, dynamic recommendations, and advertising.
Category/listing archetype. Represents server-rendered browse content and dense link lists.
Authentication form. Represents account and sensitive input handling; empty submission was exercised.
Primary transit-search destination linked from global navigation. Direct navigation was attempted and returned a CloudFront 403.
Map application destination linked from global navigation. Direct navigation was attempted and returned a CloudFront 403; mobile layout lacked viewport metadata.
Place-detail archetype selected from a homepage recommendation. Direct navigation was attempted and returned a CloudFront 403.

findings.summary: The interface does not follow the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-preference screenshot is still white and green, and computed color-scheme is normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define dark surface, text, control, icon and browser-chrome colors with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Several text colors fail minimum contrast and contrast preference does not materially adapt them.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports ratios of 3.16, 3.62 and 3.87 where 4.5:1 is required; the prefers-contrast capture remains visually unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Use stronger foreground tokens and add a prefers-contrast: more override for subtle text and control boundaries.

findings.summary: Route changes use ordinary full navigations with no authored transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The DOM/CSS probe found no view-transition rules, while route links navigate to abrupt full-page states including raw 403 pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-origin cross-document View Transitions for eligible route changes, with a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: The large, dense global chrome remains static instead of adapting as the user scrolls.
findings.evidence: Homepage screenshots and CSS inspection show persistent multi-row navigation; no scroll-state or scroll-timeline rules were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the header after scrolling and preserve a compact task-oriented affordance using scroll-state queries with a fallback.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks a page heading/main landmark and presents many competing navigation choices.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero H1 and no main landmark; the first viewport includes multiple dense navigation rows and ads around the route form.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a clear H1 and main landmark, simplify the first-view hierarchy, and guide focus to the route task after navigation.

findings.summary: Rich controls rely on custom Vue modal/autocomplete code rather than native semantic overlay primitives.
findings.evidence: The probe found zero dialog, popover and details elements, while resource inspection found vue-js-modal and custom modal assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal flows, popover for transient suggestions and details for disclosures, preserving accessible focus and light-dismiss.

findings.summary: Navigation, promotional links and advertising crowd the primary route-search task.
findings.evidence: The desktop first view devotes three navigation rows and an ad banner to chrome; the mobile view clips the same desktop composition.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse secondary navigation into progressive disclosure and defer nonessential promotional and ad content until after the core task.

findings.summary: The homepage is a fixed desktop canvas on a 360 px viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout metrics report scrollWidth 769 versus visual viewport 360, producing 409 px overflow; controls and navigation are cut off in the screenshot.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace fixed widths with intrinsic/fluid sizing, ensure responsive viewport behavior, and test all key routes at 320 to 400 px.

findings.summary: Components do not adapt to their available container.
findings.evidence: The live stylesheet probe found zero container rules, while the route form and nav remain desktop-sized in a 360 px viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Define containment on reusable shells and use size container queries to reflow route controls and navigation locally.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible on several primary controls.
findings.evidence: The focus probe reports outline-style none on origin/destination inputs, date/time controls and the icon-only search button; the button also has no accessible name.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide strong :focus-visible styles, accessible names for icon controls, and maintain at least 44 by 44 CSS-pixel touch targets.

findings.summary: Representative transit, map and place-detail destinations fail with CloudFront 403 responses.
findings.evidence: Direct attempts to /transfer/, /maps/poi and the selected POI all produced raw CloudFront 403 pages, preventing end-to-end flow completion in this run.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit CDN/WAF rules and reproduce with normal browser navigation; ensure primary linked routes consistently return the intended application and preserve task context.

findings.summary: Failure states expose infrastructure text without useful recovery.
findings.evidence: All three failed destinations show the generic CloudFront “request could not be satisfied” page with no retry, back, status or support action tailored to NAVITIME.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a branded error state with retry, back-to-search, status and support options, while retaining the user’s route inputs.

findings.summary: Loading performance misses the good LCP and responsiveness ranges.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.3 s, TBT 530 ms, Speed Index 12.3 s and TTI 32.6 s; an independent trace observed LCP 7.56 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP element, delay nonessential third parties, break up tasks and measure field INP/LCP/CLS.

findings.summary: Script execution and delayed interactivity are excessive.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 530 ms TBT and 32.6 s TTI; the HAR contains 61 scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or defer nonessential scripts, split long work, schedule by priority, and isolate expensive work off the main thread where suitable.

findings.summary: The page has a heavy request graph and weak caching for important resources.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 252 requests and 3.19 MB, seven parser-inserted stylesheets, multiple synchronous first-party scripts, and missing cache headers on large images/scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer noncritical styles/scripts, set immutable caching on versioned assets, compress text and prioritize the LCP resource.

findings.summary: Third-party and legacy script volume dominates the load.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 61 scripts and 69 third-party origins; resources include Vue 2-era plugins, multiple analytics stacks and ad bidders.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory code by user value, remove duplicate analytics/ad vendors, conditionally load secondary features and modernize legacy bundles.

findings.summary: Key controls and images lack accessible names or labels.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags unnamed links and images without alt; the custom probe finds an unnamed icon search button and unlabeled controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Add programmatic labels/names, meaningful alt or empty decorative alt, and use native semantics before ARIA.

findings.summary: Text and UI colors fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports multiple failures, including #32a632 on white at 3.16:1 and grey text at 3.62:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use accessible color tokens meeting at least 4.5:1 for normal text and verify interactive states.

findings.summary: Document structure and focus treatment do not support efficient keyboard or assistive-technology navigation.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports no main landmark; the homepage has no H1; multiple focused inputs and links have no visible outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one main landmark and logical H1, preserve heading order, and make :focus-visible clear on every control.

findings.summary: Mobile text and controls are clipped rather than reflowed.
findings.evidence: At 360 px the 769 px layout cuts navigation labels, the route form and the search button off-screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt fluid text/layout sizing, wrap navigation intentionally, and constrain line lengths without clipping at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Key surfaces do not reflow for a narrow/zoomed viewport.
findings.evidence: Homepage overflow is 409 px at 360 px; the maps route has no viewport meta and renders a 980 px desktop surface scaled down.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore viewport metadata on every template and meet WCAG reflow at 320 CSS px without two-dimensional scrolling.

findings.summary: The page logs runtime, CORS and network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse records a third-party console.error, a blocked CORS XHR and failed/400 resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix first-party request failures, remove failing vendors and contain third-party errors so expected failures do not pollute the console.

findings.summary: Image markup and rendering are not consistently sound.
findings.evidence: The image audit finds 53 images without both dimensions, 23 oversized images and 35 legacy-format images; Lighthouse detects a distorted 864x1079 image shown at 188x140.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, preserve crop intent with object-fit, and deliver responsive modern-format sources.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and aging client libraries remain in the dependency surface.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports deprecated Topics and Shared Storage usage from ad scripts; resources include axios 0.19.2 and several old Vue plugins.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated vendor integrations, update supported libraries, and continuously monitor DevTools deprecations and vulnerabilities.

findings.summary: The public site is not consistently mobile friendly across templates.
findings.evidence: The homepage has 409 px horizontal overflow and /maps/poi lacks viewport metadata, despite crawlable href links.
findings.suggestedFix: Make every public template responsive and include a valid viewport meta tag while retaining real descriptive href links.

findings.summary: The homepage exposes no social preview or structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found zero Open Graph tags and zero JSON-LD blocks on the public homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph/Twitter metadata and appropriate Organization/WebSite JSON-LD matching visible content.

findings.summary: Baseline transport defenses and cookie attributes are missing.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP and HSTS are absent; all 25 observed first-party cookies were flagged insecure and many use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforcing CSP and HSTS, mark HTTPS cookies Secure, use Lax/Strict by default and reserve SameSite=None for necessary cross-site cases.

findings.summary: The homepage has an exceptionally broad tracking and advertising footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker audit found 69 third-party origins and 25 known tracker domains; Lighthouse found 39 third-party cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a data inventory, remove redundant vendors, gate nonessential trackers behind informed consent, shorten retention and batch minimal analytics.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only and lacks phishing-resistant options.
findings.evidence: The sign-in probe found a password field and no WebAuthn/Passkey usage; no permission prompt on load was detected.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and authentication alongside recovery-safe fallback, and retain in-context permission prompting.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are largely absent.
findings.evidence: Headers lack CSP/frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, HSTS, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; only nosniff is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Set CSP with frame-ancestors, HSTS, strict referrer policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; evaluate Trusted Types for script-heavy surfaces.

findings.summary: Most homepage content is unavailable to non-JavaScript clients.
findings.evidence: Discoverability comparison reports only 8% raw-HTML coverage; the crawler screenshot contains global chrome but omits the route task and recommendations, while category coverage is 100%.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the primary route form and essential homepage content, then enhance suggestions and live data with JavaScript.

findings.summary: Network/HTTP failures fall through to raw infrastructure pages.
findings.evidence: Three representative destinations returned bare CloudFront 403 pages with no application recovery controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Map CDN and application failures to branded, accessible recovery states with retry, back and preserved task data.

findings.summary: The Japanese document declares language but its CSS is not writing-mode adaptable.
findings.evidence: The probe confirms html lang=ja but finds zero logical-property rules in loaded stylesheets; the clipped mobile layout relies on physical desktop geometry.
findings.suggestedFix: Use logical inline/block properties and validate translated expansion and RTL/writing-mode behavior while preserving lang per localized page.

findings.summary: Empty sign-in submission does not reveal clear, visible recovery guidance.
findings.evidence: After an empty submit attempt the screenshot is visually unchanged; login/password inputs also omit autocomplete tokens and rely on placeholders.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, associate errors with fields, announce a summary, retain input and focus the first invalid field.

findings.summary: Route and sign-in inputs disable or omit useful autocomplete semantics.
findings.evidence: Homepage route inputs use autocomplete=off; sign-in ID/password fields have empty autocomplete values instead of username/current-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Use standardized autocomplete tokens and only disable autofill for fields where stored personal data is genuinely inappropriate.

findings.summary: The account flow relies on password authentication without a visible phishing-resistant option.
findings.evidence: The sign-in page offers NAVITIME ID/password and Yahoo login; the probe found no WebAuthn/Passkey capability.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkeys, make session persistence and recovery consequences explicit, and keep account cancellation and reauthentication findable.

findings.summary: Images are frequently oversized, unresponsive or legacy-format.
findings.evidence: The image audit finds 23 oversized images, 18 without srcset and 35 legacy-format images; one 334 KB image lacks cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive sources, size them to rendered slots, preserve dimensions and lazy-load below-fold media.

findings.summary: Advertising and analytics create substantial background network work.
findings.evidence: The homepage makes 252 requests, including 90 XHR/fetch calls, across 69 third-party origins, with several failed or redirected ad-tech requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant vendors, defer background fetches until needed, batch analytics and stop work when the page is hidden.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts and advertising are disproportionate to the navigation task.
findings.evidence: The HAR transfers 3.19 MB with 61 scripts; the tracker inventory finds 69 third-party origins and 25 known trackers.
findings.suggestedFix: Set enforceable budgets for third-party requests/bytes, load ads after the core task, and require measurable user value for every vendor.

taskList.title: Restore mobile reflow and input accessibility
Reduce and govern trackers, cookies and third parties
Deploy security headers and secure cookie defaults
Make primary linked journeys reliable and recoverable
Cut critical-path scripts, requests and uncached assets
Repair semantics, landmarks, labels, focus and contrast
Progressively render the homepage core task
Modernize sign-in assistance, errors and passkeys
Add preference-aware theming and simplify chrome
